gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 + 2×200W Solar bundle costs $1,499 on bluettipower.com, $198 less than buying the station ($899) and two SP200L panels ($798) separately, or that the two panels' combined open-circuit voltage in series (2 × 24.6 V = 49.2 V) fits inside the station's 12–60 V solar input, while wiring them in parallel would put their combined short-circuit current (2 × 10.8 A = 21.6 A) above the input's 20 A maximum.
standout_why: Compared against basc.pnnl.gov (the page ChatGPT cited in both chats) and itechguides.com/can-a-portable-power-station-keep-a-refrigerator-running-during-an-outage/ (cited in the second chat). PNNL covers sizing (EnergyGuide kWh/365, startup at up to 3× running watts, side-by-side units needing up to 2,000 W to start) and says 1–2 kWh batteries with PV can run a fridge 'for many hours'. It names no panel, wiring, cable or bundle. itechguides gives solar wattage in only two product blurbs (S2000 400 W, Delta 3 Classic 500 W) and does not mention series/parallel, voltage limits, MC4/XT60 cables, bundles or buying from one store. ChatGPT's own answer showed the Elite 200 V2 at $899 with no panel. The bundle saving and the series-wiring fit are new and useful. They don't decide the set, because the station's sizing still comes from the fridge's watts.
kit_items: Power station: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 (2,073.6 Wh, 2,600 W rated, LFP). Its 2,073.6 Wh sits in the 2,000–3,000 Wh range ChatGPT gave for 16–24 hours, and it costs $899, $50 less than the fridge-branded FridgePower ($949, 2,016 Wh, 1,800 W), with more capacity and output.

Solar recharge for outages longer than one battery: 2× BLUETTI SP200L 200 W panels. Each has 24.6 V Voc and 10.8 A Isc, so two in series reach 49.2 V, inside the Elite 200 V2's 12–60 V / 20 A / 1,000 W max input. Buy them as the store's bundle SKU, not separately.

Panel-to-station cable: BLUETTI Solar Charging Cable (20A MC4 to XT60), $29. Add it only if the bundle doesn't include one: the Elite 200 V2 'In the Box' list has no solar cable, and the bundle page doesn't itemize its contents (see unsourced).
Budget alternative in the same store: Elite 100 V2 + 200W bundle, $699 vs $898 bought separately (1,024 Wh, 1,800 W, 1,000 W solar input).
